Title: Carrier Certification Manager
Description:
**About Eagle Wireless**
Eagle Wireless is building the connective tissue of the physical world.
  
  
Every connected car, every industrial sensor, every IoT device that needs to talk to the cloud reliably and securely — that’s where we come in. We design and deliver cellular modules and connectivity solutions that automotive, and IoT companies trust to work for years, in the field, without compromise.
  
  
Our teams span North America, Europe, and APAC, giving you the chance to collaborate with world-class engineers and go-to-market experts solving hard problems at global scale — from cybersecurity and supply chain resilience to regulatory compliance across dozens of markets.
  
  
If you want your work to matter in a world that’s rapidly connecting everything, and you want to do it alongside people obsessed with getting the hard stuff right, Eagle Wireless is where that happens.
  
  
**About The Role**
The Carrier Certification Manager will own Eagle's end-to-end carrier certification program across the US and Canada. This includes managing active certification projects, building and maintaining carrier relationships, and working cross-functionally with product, engineering, and sales to ensure Eagle's modules achieve and maintain certification across all major networks. This role is essential to Eagle's product commercialization timeline and go-to-market readiness.
  
  
**Key Requirements**

* Manage active carrier certification programs across AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile (US), and Telus, Rogers, Bell (Canada), ensuring on-time completion.
* Serve as Eagle's primary point of contact with carrier certification teams and labs; build and maintain trusted relationships with carrier ecosystem managers.
* Coordinate pre-certification activities: lab selection, test plan development, sample preparation, and firmware readiness in collaboration with engineering and product teams.
* Own the certification project tracker and communicate progress, risks, and timelines to product management and executive leadership.
* Manage certification costs, budgets, and vendor relationships (third-party test labs, certification bodies).
* Oversee PTCRB, GCF, FCC/IC, and ISED submissions that feed into carrier certification eligibility.
* Monitor carrier certification policy changes, new requirements, and network evolution (e.g., 5G Standalone, Network Slicing) and proactively update Eagle's certification strategy.
* Support the sales team by clearly communicating certification status and timelines for customer RFQs and design-in decisions.
* Develop and maintain certification documentation, including test reports and compliance records.

**Required Qualifications**

* 5+ years of experience in carrier certification, regulatory compliance, or technical program management within the wireless, module, or device ecosystem.
* Direct experience managing AT&T, Verizon, or T-Mobile certification processes; Canadian carrier experience is a plus.
* Understanding of PTCRB, GCF, FCC/IC certification frameworks and their interplay with carrier certification.
* Strong project management skills; ability to run multiple certification programs in parallel.
* Excellent cross-functional communication skills with engineering, product, and sales stakeholders.
* Experience with cellular module certification specifically (as opposed to device/handset only).
* Familiarity with 5G NR certification requirements and how they differ from LTE.
* Knowledge of ISED (Canada), FirstNet, and MVNO certification requirements.
* Experience working with third-party test labs.
* Flexible to attend occasional early-morning or evening calls to coordinate with teams in Asia (UTC+8).
* Willing to travel occasionally to carrier or third-party laboratories to provide on-site support as needed.

**What We Offer**
**Our work environment is collaborative, and we offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, which includes medical/dental/vision, generous PTO and paid parental leave programs.**
**Eagle Wireless recognizes the importance of forming inclusive teams to foster an environment where creative solutions are made for our clients, and all have the opportunity to thrive and succeed. We encourage candidates from a variety of backgrounds to apply to be a part of our team.**

Title: Director Operations (Hospital)
Description:
**Director Operations (Hospital) | Dubai, UAE**

**About Us**

Our client is a new premium tertiary hospital in Dubai Healthcare City, opening in 2027. Backed by Scope Investment, it is being developed as an academic medical centre for the region. Advanced gastroenterology is its flagship programme, supported by a growing range of specialist services and centres of excellence. The hospital combines the latest medical technology with an academic approach to care, teaching and research, in a state-of-the-art building with premium design and a seamless digital patient journey. Care is physician-led and organised around the patient, and the hospital is designed to meet JCI standards from day one. Joining us now means helping to shape a new hospital from the ground up and building your career in an academic setting, with teaching, research, and fellowship opportunities alongside clinical practice.

**About the Role**

We are seeking an accomplished hospital operations leader with strong UAE healthcare experience to lead operational readiness, commissioning, service delivery, and continuous improvement as the hospital progresses towards opening and full 24/7 operations.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead hospital commissioning, phased activation, go-live and post-opening operational stabilisation
* Oversee day-to-day clinical support, administrative and non-clinical operations
* Establish operational governance, process ownership, KPIs, SLAs and executive performance reporting
* Optimize patient flow, capacity, productivity, service quality and resource utilisation.
* Develop the Operations Command Centre and real-time operational management capability
* Drive operational excellence, process improvement and measurable benefits realisation
* Lead operational requirements for HIS implementation, digitalisation, automation and responsible AI adoption
* Ensure operational compliance and readiness for DHA licensing, JCI accreditation, audits and patient-safety requirements
* Partner with Finance and clinical leaders on budgets, cost optimisation, service-line growth and revenue performance
* Oversee patient experience, support services, vendor performance, business continuity and emergency preparedness
* Build, lead and develop a high-performing Operations team for the new hospital

**Ideal Candidate**

* 12+ years of progressive experience in hospital operations, operational excellence or healthcare transformation, preferably in Dubai or the wider UAE.
* 5+ years of senior leadership experience in hospital operations or operational transformation.
* Strong UAE hospital experience with sound knowledge of DHA requirements and JCI standards
* Hands-on involvement in commissioning, opening, expanding or transforming a hospital
* Demonstrated success in patient flow, capacity planning, workforce productivity, cost optimisation and service improvement
* Experience with HIS implementation, performance dashboards, digital workflows, automation or AI-enabled operations
* Master's degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration or a related field is preferred

If you are a healthcare operations leader who would like to shape the operating model of a new hospital from the ground up, we would be pleased to hear from you.

**Ideal Candidate**

**We are particularly interested in hospital operations leaders who have successfully contributed to commissioning or opening a new hospital in the UAE and can establish robust operational systems, governance and performance controls from the ground up.**

Candidates should demonstrate direct responsibility for operational readiness, patient flow, process improvement, digital enablement and multidisciplinary service delivery. This is an opportunity to do more than manage daily operations. You will help shape the operational foundation, culture, and patient journey of a new academic hospital from commissioning through full 24/7 operations.

**Please note: This position requires extensive hospital operations and commissioning experience. Applicants without relevant healthcare and hospital experience will not be considered.**

Title: Manager Strategic Contracts
Description:

Safety Power is a Canadian designer and manufacturer of high-technology emissions control equipment supplied to some of the world’s largest companies, including end users such as Microsoft, Meta, Google and AWS. We are seeking an experienced Manager for strategic contracts. The technical nature of the company’s business requires an individual with an engineering degree and experience dealing with complex contracts. An Engineering degree is required and an MBA degree would be an asset. This position reports directly to the CFO and has visibility into important contracts that are critical to the company.

The successful candidate will personally review and redline sophisticated contracts; negotiate directly with customers, supplier and other counterparties; summarize salient points for discussion with the executive team; and liaise with external counsel where appropriate. Sound business judgement and acumen is important as the Manager, Strategic Contracts must negotiate on behalf of Safety Power and understand which issues require elevation to the executive team. Strong familiarity with AI tools is required.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Lead review, drafting, redlining and negotiation of complex, high-value customer contracts, master supply and service agreements, procurement terms and other commercial arrangements, including agreements with joint venture multinational counterparties.

* Advise on supplier contracts, confidentiality arrangements, joint ventures and other Canadian and U.S. transactions, utilizing external specialists when appropriate.
* Prepare concise executive summaries of key risks, proposed compromises and unresolved issues; escalate material departures from approved positions and secure final executive approval.
* Collaborate closely with sales, finance, engineering, project management and operations; develop templates, negotiating playbooks and efficient contract-review procedures.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering from a recognized university (mandatory).

**Preferred Experience**

* Past experience with manufacturing, engineered equipment, energy, industrial projects or technical services.

**Ideal Candidate**

A practical business person with an engineer’s grasp of technical risk. This person can work through a complex customer agreement, distinguish consequential issues from routine drafting points, propose commercially realistic solutions and bring a negotiation to closure. They are comfortable writing redlines themselves, using outside resources selectively and consulting senior leadership on material decisions.

**What We Offer**

* $140,000–$180,000 CAD base salary, plus potential performance bonus.
* Substantial autonomy, direct access to senior executive leadership and influence over major commercial transactions.
* Exposure to multinational customers and Canadian and U.S. operations.

Title: Metadata and Localization Lead, Global Product Delivery
Description:
TELLING CAPTIVATING STORIES TO AUDIENCES EVERYWHERE
  
**Blue Ant Media (TSX:** BAMI) is an international streamer, production studio, advertising sales and rights-management business. The company operates a diverse portfolio of free streaming and pay TV channels internationally, including Love Nature, Cottage Life, Smithsonian Channel Canada, BBC Earth Canada, HauntTV, Homeful, and Love Pets, as well as the subscription streaming service MagellanTV. Its studio business produces and distributes a wide range of premium content across key genres for streaming and broadcast platforms worldwide. Blue Ant Media is headquartered in Toronto, with a presence in Los Angeles, New York, Miami, Singapore, London, Washington, Sydney, Halifax, and Ottawa. blueantmedia.com⼁Instagram⼁LinkedIn
  
Our employees are passionate experts in all of our business areas. They are fanatical about creating outstanding content and experiences, and about delivering them on new and evolving platforms. We actively seek new employees who embody our core values. We want them to think big, act with purpose, celebrate creativity, do the right thing, respect one another, and succeed together. We attract creative talents who are optimistic about the evolving future of content and who take pride in recognizing opportunities where others see challenges. At Blue Ant Media, we give them the flexibility to think like entrepreneurs, take ownership of their projects, take risks, and embrace innovation in a rapidly evolving media landscape. Our team members excel at collaborating with internal and external partners by building trusting, respectful working relationships.
  
  
Metadata and Localization Lead, Global Product Delivery
  
The Metadata and Localization Lead is responsible for the accuracy, consistency, maintenance and operational readiness of program metadata across Blue Ant Media's distribution platforms, alongside the coordination of localization operations.
  
This replacement role oversees metadata management, recurring program copy and FAST artwork requirements, and the operational coordination of dubbing, subtitling and metadata translation projects. Working closely with internal teams and external vendors, the position ensures that program information and language assets are accurately maintained, tracked and made available according to business requirements.
  
This role also contributes to workflow optimization, systems integration and automation initiatives, particularly across Airtable and Blue Lucy.
  
This role will report to the Senior Manager, Content Operations, Global Product Delivery and is a hybrid position requiring in-office attendance at our head office in Toronto for a minimum of three (3) days per week.
  
The anticipated salary range for this role is $60,000 – $65,000 per year, with final compensation determined by experience and qualifications.
  
Core Responsibilities & Duties
  
Metadata Management and Operations
  

* Oversee the organization, accuracy, consistency and completeness of program metadata across FAST, VOD, SVOD, linear and other distribution platforms.
* Establish and maintain metadata standards, operational workflows and quality-control processes.
* Coordinate program metadata intake, maintenance, updates, translations and recurring platform requirements.
* Identify and resolve metadata discrepancies, missing information and operational gaps.
* Manage recurring metadata requirements for platform launches, monthly refresh schedules and ongoing catalogue updates.
* Coordinate program copy, descriptions, FAST artwork and associated metadata requirements, including submitting recurring requests to Creative and other relevant teams through established workflows.
* Support new platform metadata setups, specification changes and template development, ensuring requirements are incorporated into existing workflows.
* Support the centralization and migration of legacy metadata into established systems and repositories.

Localization Operations and Vendor Coordination
  

* Coordinate day-to-day localization operations, including dubbing, subtitling and metadata translation, in accordance with approved requirements and production plans.
* Review monthly FAST and linear refresh schedules to identify upcoming localization requirements and prepare for recurring deliveries.
* Maintain localization trackers, language-version records, vendor quotations, production statuses and associated documentation.
* Coordinate localization requests with approved vendors, ensuring requirements, specifications, source materials and deadlines are communicated accurately and on time.
* Work closely with Content Deliveries, Media Services and relevant internal teams to ensure source files are made available to localization vendors.
* Monitor production progress, follow up on outstanding deliverables and escalate potential delays, quality concerns or operational issues.
* Update localization trackers and relevant systems upon receipt of completed language assets, maintaining accurate records of delivered materials.
* Reconcile vendor invoices against approved quotations, agreed rates, completed deliveries and final production costs, resolving discrepancies and routing validated invoices for approval.
* Provide operational support for localization proof-of-concept (PoC) projects, including AI-assisted localization workflows and new vendor evaluations.
* Coordinate sample preparation, testing, feedback collection and documentation of results to support technology and vendor assessments.

Systems Integration and Workflow Optimization
  

* Support the Senior Manager on relevant Airtable development, migration and implementation initiatives.
* Own the maintenance and continuous improvement of metadata and localization trackers, including their associated Airtable workflows.
* Coordinate the migration of existing metadata and localization records from Google Sheets and other legacy trackers into Airtable.
* Work with the Airtable development team to define functional requirements, test workflows and support implementation.
* Collaborate with the Blue Lucy team to ensure metadata structures, field mappings and relevant system connections support operational requirements.
* Identify opportunities to automate manual processes, improve data accuracy and eliminate duplication across systems.
* Support the development of dashboards, reporting tools and processes that improve operational visibility.
* Coordinate user acceptance testing, troubleshooting, documentation and process improvements for metadata and localization workflows.

Cross-Functional Coordination and Reporting
  

* Work collaboratively with GPD, Media Services, BAR, Acquisitions, FAST Programming, Creative, Technology and external vendors to support metadata and localization requirements.
* Maintain clear communication with stakeholders regarding project status, outstanding requirements, production timelines and operational risks.
* Coordinate metadata and localization activities across concurrent projects and recurring delivery schedules.
* Maintain operational reports covering metadata readiness, localization volumes, vendor deliveries, outstanding requests and associated costs.
* Provide regular updates to GPD management, escalating issues requiring decisions, resources or intervention.
* Contribute to the development, documentation and continuous improvement of standard operating procedures.

Key Qualifications and Experience
  

* Experience in metadata management, content operations, media distribution, localization or a related field.
* Strong understanding of metadata workflows and digital content distribution across FAST, VOD, SVOD and linear platforms.
* Excellent organizational, coordination and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple workflows and competing deadlines.
* Proficiency in Airtable, including database management, workflow tracking, interfaces and automations.
* Strong attention to detail, particularly in data management, vendor quotations, invoice reconciliation and delivery tracking.
* Excellent interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and external vendors.
* A proactive, solutions-oriented approach to identifying operational issues and improving processes.
* Experience with Blue Lucy or comparable media asset management systems is an asset.
* Familiarity with localization processes, including dubbing, subtitling and metadata translation is an asset.
* Experience supporting vendor evaluations, AI localization testing and proof-of-concept initiatives is an asset.
* Knowledge of metadata mapping, data migration and systems integration is an asset.
* Experience developing operational reporting and workflow automation solutions is an asset.

=====================================

Every day, we deliver safe and secure energy to homes, communities, and businesses, connecting people to the energy they need for their lives. Our expertise and track record position us uniquely to shape the sustainable future of our industry as the pace of change accelerates. To succeed, we must anticipate customer needs, reduce energy delivery costs, and pioneer flexible energy systems. This requires delivering on our promises and seeking opportunities for growth.

In IT and Digital, we collaborate closely with the diverse energy businesses within the National Grid group, revolutionizing operations through technology. Embracing modern methodologies and digital mindsets, we drive efficiency and bring new capabilities to internal and external customers as we lead the charge toward a carbon-free future.

Our work is critical, as National Grid powers millions of homes and businesses across the UK and US, and the technology we employ is vital to this task. The successful applicant for this position will play a crucial role in our mission, supported by our multicultural, customer-centric global team, with opportunities for professional development.

**National Grid is hiring a Head of US Operational Technology role which operates under a hybrid working model and is open to candidates based at our Waltham, MA, Syracuse, NY, and Brooklyn, NY.**

**This is a hybrid role. Employees are expected to work from their assigned office or another approved work location outside the home at least three days per week. Additional in-person attendance may be required based on role, team, and business needs.**

### **Job Purpose**

The Head of U.S. Operational Technology (OT) is a senior leadership role accountable for the safe, reliable, resilient, secure and supportable operation of the technology environments that underpin real-time electric transmission, electric distribution and gas distribution operations across Massachusetts and New York. The role reports to the VP, Head of IT&D Electric and works in close partnership with Electric and Gas Operations, Cybersecurity, Engineering, Architecture, Regulatory, Capital Delivery and other enterprise technology leaders.

The role leads a multidisciplinary organization responsible for 24x7 operational support and lifecycle stewardship of OT applications and infrastructure. The scope includes Energy Management Systems (EMS), Gas Management System (GMS), Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS), Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS), SCADA-related capabilities and the supporting network, compute, storage, database, integration and recovery environments. It also includes designated technology supporting LNG operations, physical security systems, substation controllers and substation access points.

You’ll join an established team, building on its existing strengths to deliver meaningful outcomes. Working collaboratively with colleagues and stakeholders, you’ll help shape priorities, improve ways of working, and support the team’s continued development and success.

The Head of OT leads directors responsible for application and infrastructure domains and is a key partner to control center, operations, regulatory and executive stakeholders. The role requires experienced, visible leadership during significant events; disciplined governance; strong technical judgment; and the ability to convert technical risk into clear business decisions.

### **Key Accountabilities**

**Safe, Reliable and Resilient Operations**

* Own the availability, resilience, performance, and recoverability of the OT estate.
* Establish clear 24x7 operational accountability, escalation, and decision-making.
* Lead technology response to major incidents and operational events.
* Maintain and test business continuity, disaster recovery, and recovery capabilities.
* Ensure readiness for storms, grid emergencies, outages, and critical operational events.
* Drive continuous improvement through incident analysis and root-cause elimination.

**Cybersecurity, Safety, Compliance and Risk**

* Ensure readiness and compliance with applicable regulatory and cybersecurity requirements.
* Embed safety, cyber, compliance, and risk considerations into technology decisions.
* Maintain auditable controls, remediation plans, and risk management processes.
* Provide transparent reporting on operational, technology, and compliance risks.
* Support regulatory filings, rate cases, and investment planning.

**Technology Strategy and Lifecycle Stewardship**

* Own OT technology roadmaps aligned to business, regulatory, and investment priorities.
* Proactively manage technology obsolescence and lifecycle risk.
* Drive risk-based management of patching, upgrades, vulnerabilities, capacity, and technical debt.
* Establish standards for integration, automation, observability, and platform management.
* Enable trusted operational data, analytics, and AI capabilities.

**Portfolio Prioritization and Investment Leadership**

* Own OT demand, capacity, and prioritization across operations and capital programs.
* Lead transparent prioritization and resource trade-off decisions.
* Maintain credible operational and capital forecasts.
* Translate technology investments into measurable business outcomes.
* Ensure effective governance, intake, and decision-making processes.

**Enabling Capital Delivery and Operational Acceptance**

* Align OT resources to the highest-priority initiatives.
* Represent operational requirements throughout delivery and implementation.
* Ensure operational readiness before service acceptance.
* Identify and manage cross-program dependencies and risks.
* Enable smooth transition from project delivery to steady-state operations.

**Team Leadership, Capability and Culture**

* Lead and develop senior leaders across OT applications and infrastructure.
* Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Establish role clarity across internal teams, partners, and suppliers.
* Build workforce capability, succession plans, and organizational resilience.
* Ensure teams are trained and prepared to meet operational and compliance obligations.
* Strengthen collaboration across OT, IT&D, Operations, Cybersecurity, Engineering, and Capital Delivery.

**Stakeholder, Executive and Vendor Leadership**

* Build trusted partnerships with operational and business leaders.
* Provide clear, data-driven reporting to executives and governance forums.
* Lead strategic supplier performance, accountability, and risk management.
* Challenge decisions that increase operational risk or reduce delivery credibility.
* Act as the senior escalation point for critical operational and technology decisions.

### **Qualifications**

* Senior leadership experience within utility OT, critical infrastructure, or another highly regulated 24x7 operating environment.
* Demonstrated accountability for mission-critical services, operational risk, incident management, and service performance.
* Deep expertise in one or more OT domains (EMS, ADMS, DERMS, GMS, SCADA, OMS) with the ability to lead across a broader technology landscape.
* Experience leading multidisciplinary teams spanning applications, infrastructure, networks, integration, databases, and operational support.
* Strong understanding of cybersecurity, resilience, and regulatory frameworks, including NERC CIP and TSA requirements.
* Proven track record supporting large-scale transformation while maintaining operational stability.
* Experience managing strategic vendors, managed services, and system integrators.
* Strong financial, workforce, and portfolio management capabilities.
* Excellent executive communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

Title: Shelter Manager
Description:
The Shelter Manager is responsible for the overall administrative and operational management of Animal Orphanage, ensuring the effective daily operation of the facility, supervision and administration of staff, financial and administrative coordination, customer service, regulatory compliance, and maintenance of the shelter's buildings, grounds, and vehicles.

This position serves as the senior operational manager of Animal Orphanage and provides leadership, direction, and oversight of shelter-wide operations. The Shelter Manager is responsible for coordinating the work of the Animal Care Manager and other shelter employees, establishing operational priorities, and ensuring that organizational policies and procedures are consistently followed.

The Shelter Manager has overall operational authority and final day-to-day decision-making responsibility, subject to the authority of the Board of Directors. The Shelter Manager reports directly to the President and Vice President of the Board of Directors.

JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Shelter Operations and Administration

* Oversees the day-to-day administrative and operational functions of the shelter to ensure efficient and consistent operations.
* Provides overall operational leadership and direction to the Animal Care Manager and other shelter employees.
* Establishes organizational priorities and coordinates responsibilities between the Animal Care Manager and other staff to ensure effective shelter operations.
* Develops, implements, and monitors operational procedures and policies for staff and volunteers in collaboration with the Animal Care Manager.
* Ensures shelter operations comply with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, licensing requirements, and organizational policies.
* Responsible for the completion and submission of required administrative paperwork and documentation necessary to maintain applicable licenses, certifications, and regulatory compliance.
* Maintains accurate and organized administrative records, files, and documentation.
* Ensures shelter management software and applicable administrative records are current and maintained, coordinating with the Animal Care Manager regarding animal-related records.
* Oversees website administration and ensures public-facing shelter information is accurate and current.
* Coordinates with other shelters, rescues, municipalities, and outside organizations as needed.
* Develops and maintains positive working relationships with Animal Control, law enforcement, local veterinarians, volunteers, foster families, and other stakeholders.
* Ensures the public receives accurate, consistent, and professional information regarding shelter services, policies, and operations.

Staff Supervision and Human Resources

* Responsible for the overall supervision and administration of shelter employees.
* Oversees employee recruitment, hiring coordination, onboarding, and orientation in collaboration with the Board President and Vice President.
* Develops and maintains staff schedules and assigns work responsibilities to ensure adequate operational coverage.
* Establishes overall staffing priorities and coordinates scheduling with the Animal Care Manager.
* Monitors staffing levels and evaluates operational needs to ensure appropriate allocation of personnel.
* Evaluates the need to fill vacant positions and recommends changes to staffing structure and allocated positions as needed.
* Oversees employee performance management, including evaluations, coaching, corrective action, and documentation.
* Addresses employee relations matters and works to maintain a professional, respectful, and productive workplace.
* Coordinates staff training and ensures employees receive appropriate instruction regarding workplace policies, safety procedures, and job responsibilities.
* Monitors attendance, timekeeping, and employee leave records.
* Coordinates payroll submissions and related documentation with the bookkeeper.
* Communicates staffing concerns, performance issues, and significant personnel matters to the Board President or Vice President as appropriate.
* Works collaboratively with the Animal Care Manager to address animal care staffing needs, training, performance, and scheduling.
* Establishes clear supervisory responsibilities and ensures employees receive consistent direction and understand reporting relationships.

Financial and Administrative Coordination

* Works directly with the bookkeeper to coordinate and maintain accurate administrative and financial records.
* Coordinates payroll submissions, mileage reimbursements, employee time records, and other documentation required for bookkeeping and payroll processing.
* Tracks and monitors routine shelter expenses and communicates financial or purchasing concerns to the Board President or Vice President.
* Coordinates purchasing and maintains appropriate inventory of administrative supplies, office equipment, and general facility supplies.
* Works with the Animal Care Manager to coordinate animal care supply and equipment purchasing needs.
* Ensures purchases are made in accordance with established budgets, purchasing procedures, and Board authorization requirements.
* Maintains accurate records of purchases, invoices, receipts, deposits, and other administrative transactions.
* Assists with budget preparation, expense tracking, and financial reporting as requested.
* Receives, processes, and records donations and other payments, including entering donation information into the organization's donor management platform.
* Prepares deposits and maintains accurate supporting documentation.
* Coordinates deposit preparation with the Animal Care Manager to ensure cash and checks are independently counted and deposit totals verified before submission.
* Does not assume responsibility for the Board Treasurer's financial oversight or the bookkeeper's accounting and reconciliation responsibilities.

Facility and Vehicle Maintenance

* Ensures the shelter facility, buildings, grounds, and vehicles are maintained in a safe, sanitary, and functional condition.
* Regularly inspects shelter property to identify needed repairs, maintenance, and safety improvements.
* Coordinates necessary maintenance, repairs, and service work for buildings, grounds, equipment, and the shelter-owned vehicle.
* Coordinates outside contractors and service providers as needed.
* Monitors facility maintenance needs and communicates significant repairs, expenses, or safety concerns to the Board President or Vice President.
* Maintains records of facility maintenance, repairs, and vehicle servicing.
* Ensures appropriate safety and sanitation standards are maintained throughout the facility in collaboration with the Animal Care Manager.
* Coordinates maintenance of equipment and supplies necessary for daily shelter operations.

Customer Service and Public Relations

* Oversees customer service standards and ensures inquiries from the public are handled professionally and in a timely manner.
* Addresses customer complaints, concerns, and escalated issues involving shelter operations and services.
* Ensures staff communicate shelter policies and procedures accurately and consistently.
* Oversees the administrative aspects of public inquiries, including adoption-related communications and follow-up.
* Works with the Animal Care Manager to ensure adoption applicants receive timely communication and accurate information.
* Supports positive relationships with municipal partners, community organizations, donors, volunteers, and the public.

Safety, Compliance, and Incident Reporting

Safety and Incident Reporting

* Ensures workplace safety policies and procedures are implemented and followed by all employees and volunteers throughout shelter operations.
* Identifies and addresses potential safety hazards involving employees, volunteers, visitors, animals, facilities, vehicles, and shelter operations.
* Ensures appropriate safety procedures are followed regarding hazardous materials, chemicals, equipment, and other workplace hazards.
* Completes and maintains administrative incident documentation as necessary.
* Oversees reporting and follow-up for operational incidents involving employees, volunteers, visitors, facilities, vehicles, and shelter operations, in coordination with the Animal Care Manager when animal care is involved.
* Ensures required incident reports are completed, appropriate notifications are made, and corrective or follow-up actions are addressed.
* Ensures significant workplace injuries, animal-related incidents, bites, escapes, safety concerns, regulatory issues, and operational emergencies are promptly communicated to the Board President or Vice President.
* Works collaboratively with the Animal Care Manager to investigate incidents, identify contributing factors, and implement appropriate corrective measures.

Cross-Training and Operational Coverage

* Develops and maintains working knowledge of the Animal Care Manager's essential responsibilities to provide operational coverage during absences, vacations, or other staffing needs.
* Cross-trains with the Animal Care Manager on essential animal care procedures, shelter operations, animal-related recordkeeping, and other responsibilities necessary to maintain continuity of operations.
* Provides reasonable assistance with animal care and other responsibilities outside the primary area of administrative and operational oversight when necessary to maintain shelter operations.
* Coordinates with the Animal Care Manager to ensure ongoing responsibilities, outstanding issues, and time-sensitive matters are communicated and addressed during periods of absence.
* When providing coverage, operates within established policies, procedures, and delegated authority. Veterinary and medical decisions must remain within the scope of appropriate veterinary direction and professional judgment.
* Retains overall operational authority and coordinates decisions requiring management oversight during periods when the Animal Care Manager is unavailable.
* Communicates significant decisions, operational concerns, and matters requiring additional authority to the Board President and Vice President.

Reporting and Board Communication

* Provides regular updates regarding shelter operations, staffing, administrative matters, facility needs, and significant operational concerns.
* Prepares and submits operational reports for monthly Board meetings.
* Serves as the primary management contact for routine operational communication with the Board President and Vice President.
* Communicates significant changes in staffing, operational needs, and facility conditions to the Board President and Vice President.
* Assists with the development and implementation of organizational policies, procedures, and operational improvements.
* Maintains appropriate confidentiality regarding employee, applicant, donor, financial, and organizational information.
* Other duties as assigned by the Board President and Vice President.

AUTHORITY AND REPORTING RELATIONSHIP

The Shelter Manager serves as the senior operational manager of Animal Orphanage and reports directly to the President and Vice President of the Board of Directors.

The Shelter Manager has overall responsibility for the daily operation of the shelter and final day-to-day decision-making authority regarding operational priorities, staffing and scheduling, administrative matters, customer service, facility operations, and coordination between departments, subject to established organizational policies, approved budgets, and the authority of the Board of Directors.

The Animal Care Manager reports directly to the Shelter Manager and has primary responsibility and decision-making authority over daily animal care operations and the direction of animal care staff within established policies and veterinary guidance.

The Shelter Manager is responsible for coordinating the work of both management positions, resolving operational disagreements, and ensuring organizational priorities are met. This authority does not eliminate the Animal Care Manager's responsibility or professional judgment regarding animal welfare and daily animal care practices. Veterinary medical decisions must remain consistent with veterinary direction.

Significant animal welfare, safety, regulatory, personnel, financial, or other organizational concerns must be elevated to the Board President or Vice President as appropriate. The Board retains authority over organizational governance, policies, budgets, and major personnel decisions.

HOURS

40 hours per week. Regular schedule is 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Hours may occasionally vary based on operational needs. Hours may not be flexed prior to 7:00 a.m., with the exception of days requiring early morning operational responsibilities.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE

Shelter Operations: Knowledge of animal shelter operations, applicable federal, state, and local laws, codes, ordinances, policies, and procedures relevant to the operation of an animal shelter.

Supervision and Human Resources: Knowledge of leadership techniques, principles, and procedures to recruit, train, supervise, schedule, evaluate, and manage employees. Knowledge of employee relations, performance management, and workplace policies.

Financial and Administrative Management: Knowledge of basic accounting principles, purchasing procedures, expense tracking, payroll coordination, recordkeeping, and administrative practices.

Facility and Safety Management: Knowledge of occupational hazards, safety precautions, facility maintenance practices, and applicable safety regulations related to maintaining a safe and sanitary workplace.

Customer Service: Knowledge of principles and processes for providing professional customer service, establishing service standards, resolving complaints, and maintaining positive relationships with the public.

REQUIRED SKILLS

Computer Skills: Proficiency with personal computers, word processing, spreadsheets, email, website administration, shelter management software, and related programs.

Judgment and Decision Making: Ability to evaluate operational needs, establish priorities, anticipate potential problems, and make sound decisions within the scope of assigned responsibilities.

Interpersonal Relationships: Ability to develop and maintain cooperative and professional relationships with employees, board members, volunteers, vendors, municipal representatives, and other organizations.

Organization: Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple responsibilities, maintain accurate records, meet deadlines, and coordinate competing operational priorities.

Compassion: Demonstrated compassion and respect toward animals and the people who care for them. A genuine commitment to the humane philosophy and mission of Animal Orphanage is essential.

Physical Stamina: Ability to perform occasional moderately physically demanding work, including climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and lifting, carrying, pushing, or pulling objects and materials weighing 20–50 pounds.

REQUIRED ABILITIES

Communication: Excellent ability to communicate complex ideas and proposals effectively, both verbally and in writing. Ability to prepare reports, policies, procedures, and other administrative documents. Ability to listen, understand, and communicate sensitive information with tact, diplomacy, and confidentiality.

Coordination of Work: Ability to establish and implement effective administrative programs and procedures, prioritize competing responsibilities, manage schedules, and coordinate the work of multiple employees.

Financial Management: Ability to perform arithmetic, algebraic, and basic statistical applications to complete purchasing and financial transactions. Ability to understand and apply basic accounting principles and practices in the review and reporting of budget and expense information.

Leadership: Ability to provide direction, establish expectations, address performance concerns, resolve operational disagreements, and foster a professional, accountable, and cooperative workplace.

Problem Solving: Ability to identify operational challenges, evaluate available options, and implement practical solutions while recognizing when Board direction or approval is necessary.

ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES

Performance of essential functions may require exposure to adverse environmental conditions, including dirt, dust, pollen, odors, wetness, humidity, weather and temperature extremes, noise, hazardous materials, traffic hazards, bright or dim lighting, toxic agents, animal or wildlife attacks, animal and human bites, disease, pathogenic substances, and rude or irate customers.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

* High school diploma required. College-level coursework in business administration, management, human resources, or a related field preferred.
* Certificate or degree in business administration, management, or a related field preferred.
* Five years of experience in administrative, operational, or organizational management preferred.
* Two to three years of supervisory and administrative experience preferred.
* Experience in animal shelter operations or a nonprofit organization preferred.
* Demonstrated experience in staff supervision, scheduling, administrative recordkeeping, customer service, and operational coordination.
* Must have excellent oral and written communication skills.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

* Acceptable general background check, including local and state criminal history checks and sex offender registry check.
* Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
* Satisfactory results from a pre-employment medical evaluation.

* Support go / conditional go / no-go recommendations by consolidating evidence, risks, conditions and unresolved matters.

Education

* Bachelor’s degree in Asset Management, Engineering, Project Management, Operations, Facilities Management or a related discipline.
* Professional certification in asset management, project controls, assurance, governance or project management is desirable.

Experience

* Experience in asset management, governance, assurance, design review coordination, handover readiness, project controls or infrastructure delivery.
* Strong understanding of Stage Gate processes, action tracking, evidence management, risk escalation and decision support.
* Experience working with City Operations, O&M teams, delivery teams, consultants and asset management stakeholders is preferred.

Preferred Background

* Background in AM governance, operational readiness, handover, assurance, PMO or design review environments.
* Exposure to ISO 55001-aligned asset management principles, including lifecycle, value, risk and continual improvement.

Technical & Functional Expectations

* Stage Gate assurance, design review coordination and governance reporting.
* Evidence management, comment tracking, action closure and decision logs.
* Operational readiness, handover requirements, maintainability and lifecycle considerations.
* AM platform use, dashboards, exception reporting and escalation management.

Leadership Competencies

* Planning and coordination
* Stakeholder management
* Governance discipline
* Clear escalation and follow-through

Functional Competencies

* + Stage Gate monitoring
* + Design review facilitation
* + Evidence and action tracking
* + Assurance dashboards and reporting

Behavioral Competencies

* Collaboration and partnership
* Clear, concise communication
* Structured problem solving
* Attention to detail and data discipline
* Resilience through change
* Ownership and continuous improvement

Role Scope Boundary

Stage Gate Assurance & Monitoring Senior Manager accountability: coordinate AM Stage Gate assurance activities, design review inputs, evidence packs, decision logs, action tracking and reporting. The incumbent is accountable for all operational aspects of SLATE, which operates for all Sheridan users on a continuous 24x7x365 basis. Title: Senior Program Manager, Strategy and Expansion, MEATR DSP Strategy, Planning and Expansion
Description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Customers want what they need in minutes, not days. Join Amazon's Last Mile team in the Middle East, Africa and Turkey to shape how our fastest delivery services, including Amazon Now and Amazon Rush, grow and run for customers, delivery associates, Delivery Service Partners (DSPs) and Amazon.  
  
As Senior Program Manager, you will own and lead the strategic programmes that set how our Speed last mile network runs across the region. At the core is flexible capacity: designing models that let DSP capacity move up and down with demand, setting how they fit into annual and weekly planning, and getting Operations, Finance, People teams and DSP partners behind them. Your portfolio may also cover partner commercials, compliance and training, and it will change as priorities change.  
  
Many problems won't arrive well defined. You will frame them, find the ones worth solving, align senior stakeholders on a path forward and build mechanisms that make the answers scale across countries. You will also help shape the team's wider strategy and roadmap.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Set the strategy: own the multi-year capacity and growth plan for Quick Commerce and Speed, and the region's input to annual planning.
* Plan capacity: within the regional plan, build short, mid and long range plans that match DSP and delivery associate supply to demand by hour, day and season.
* Build flexible capacity: design, launch and scale flexible models alongside the fixed DSP network, with the operating, commercial and compliance framework to run them.
* Grow the channel: launch new cities, stores and countries with capacity ready before go-live.
* Improve efficiency: raise utilisation and lower cost per delivery without moving cost onto DSPs or associates.
* Build partner economics: shape DSP commercial models with Finance that work at every volume level, and lead the trade-off decisions.
* Look after delivery associates: design fair, safe, compliant schedules and lead the regional response to labour rule changes.
* Align and lead change: bring Operations, Finance, People, Legal, Tech and DSPs behind one plan, and run readiness and approvals.
* Build mechanisms: set planning tool requirements with Tech, and the metrics, guardrails and reviews that run the channel, using automation and AI.
* Lead and write: influence senior leaders, mentor PMs and analysts, and write documents that drive decisions.

  
A day in the life  
You start with yesterday's Quick Commerce and Speed performance: where capacity matched demand, where routes ran short or associates sat idle, and what it cost. Mid-morning, you join the weekly planning review to agree where flexible capacity steps in next week. You then meet a DSP owner to test a new flexible model against their margin and their associates' hours. After lunch, you work with Finance and Legal on the case for scaling it to a second country. You end the day writing for senior leaders: what the pilot showed, what you recommend and what you need from them.  
  
About the team  
This is a new role reporting to the Senior Manager, Strategy and Expansion, MEATr DSP. Quick Commerce and Speed, including Amazon Now and Amazon Rush, are delivered by DSPs, and flexible capacity is a lead theme in the region's 2027 plan. You will own Speed capacity and flexible capacity programmes across the region, planning inside the regional capacity plan and working with the Network Optimisation team, who own rate cards. You will mentor PMs and analysts and write planning papers reviewed at Director and VP level.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 2+ years of program or project management experience
* Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
* Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
* Experience owning program strategy, end-to-end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* 2+ years of driving process improvements experience
* Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field

Title: Senior Director, Field Service
Description:
EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions helping industrial, infrastructure and defense customers address critical power and operational needs. The company delivers integrated solutions that combine energy storage technologies, power electronics, software-enabled intelligence, technical expertise and comprehensive global customer support. EnerSys supports customers across communications networks, data centers, energy infrastructure, material handling, transportation, aerospace and defense — including applications where power continuity is essential. Serving customers in more than 100 countries, EnerSys helps organizations manage energy more reliably, efficiently and intelligently in complex operating environments where uptime, safety and resilience matter.

**What We’re Offering**

* Paid time off plus paid holidays
* Medical/dental/vision insurance plan
* Life insurance, short/long term disability, tuition reimbursement, flex spending, and employee stock purchase plan
* 401K plan
* Culture: We value and strive for excellence in all that we do through innovative technology by creating long lasting relationships with our stakeholders, co-workers, and customers. We continually strive to foster teamwork, engagement and enhance our employee’s skills and competence by providing appropriate training.

**Compensation Range:** 145,100-181,500 plus sales bonus

Compensation may vary based on applicant's work experience, education level, skill set, and/or location.

**Job Purpose**
---------------

EnerSys seeks a proven operations leader with a documented record of growing and improving a large, geographically dispersed service business. The Senior Director owns operating performance and P&L results for assigned field service operations across the United States and Canada, translating the Board strategy into accountable regional execution.

The role leads EFI operations serving telecom, data center, industrial and broadband customers and coordinates field delivery with the Projects organization. Success requires measurable operating improvements, leadership through transformation, and demonstrated experience launching new products and establishing profitable maintenance programs for emerging technologies.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

**Revenue Growth**  
Deliver 10.6% year-over-year revenue growth from a base of $150M through FY2031. Translate this objective into regional operating plans supported by bookings, backlog conversion, customer retention, and delivery capacity.

**Profitability**  
Meet approved P&L and cash objectives and deliver approved growth, margin, cash, and customer retention targets.

**Recurring Services**  
Assist with growing maintenance revenue across telecom, broadband, industrial, and data center accounts through new programs for emerging technologies and expanded Long-Term Service Agreements (LTSAs). Track maintenance attachment rates, renewals, and recurring revenue growth.

**Launch Execution**  
Establish field readiness for new product introductions and maintenance programs, with defined launch milestones, trained technicians, validated procedures, parts support, and customer service commitments.

**Service Scale and Customer Confidence**  
Build national coverage with local response through four regional teams and qualified partners. EnerSys employs more than 200 field service technicians. Restore bookings by delivering consistent service, strong customer scorecards, and reliable execution of the new operating model.

**Operations Leadership and Accountability**  
Lead regional directors and managers as one service organization with common standards, clear decision rights, and shared capacity. Set expectations, coach leaders, address underperformance, and build succession plans. Own execution of the operating plan and corrective actions across assigned regions.

**P&L and Financial Management**  
Own budgets, revenue and margin delivery, labor and subcontractor costs, working capital, and forecast accuracy. Review bookings, backlog, staffing, and project estimates with Finance, Sales, and regional leaders. Make resource commitments based on credible demand and operational readiness.

**Operating Governance and Tools**  
Run weekly performance reviews and a monthly operating cadence using consistent KPIs, named owners, and dated corrective actions. Enforce Procore and field service system adoption, accurate reporting, and standard workflows. Monitor utilization, schedule performance, rework, safety, job closure, and customer outcomes.

**Customer Growth and Retention**  
Partner with Sales and Service Solutions leaders to restore bookings, expand national accounts, and convert installed equipment into recurring service contracts. Validate scope, pricing assumptions, staffing, and service levels before commitments. Own operational escalations and customer recovery plans.

**New Product Launches**  
Lead service readiness with Product Management, Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain from pilot through commercial launch. Validate installation, commissioning, diagnostics, tooling, technician certification, spare parts, warranty support, and escalation paths. Use formal readiness reviews and field feedback before expanding deployment.

**Workforce and Partner Capacity**  
Build regional capacity plans and a qualified subcontractor network aligned to demand. Advance the training center and apprenticeship program, military and trade recruiting, technical certifications, and leadership development. Hold partners to the same safety, quality, and customer standards as internal teams.

**Project Delivery and Risk Management**  
Coordinate with the Projects organization and PMO on staffing, schedules, change control, closeout, and transition to maintenance. Ensure repeatable field execution and timely escalation of delivery, financial, and contractual risks. Maintain clear ownership between field operations and project management.

**Qualifications**
------------------

**This position requires supervisory experience**

* **Proven operations leadership.** At least 10 years of progressively responsible field service or technical service operations leadership, with demonstrated success leading regional managers and geographically dispersed teams. Candidates must provide measurable examples of revenue growth, margin improvement and sustained operating performance.
* **P&L ownership at scale.** Demonstrated responsibility for a service P&L of $200 million or more in annual revenue across multiple regions or lines of business, including budgeting, forecasting, cost management and working capital accountability.
* **Transformation and execution.** A record of implementing standard operating processes, KPI governance and management accountability across a large service organization. Demonstrated ability to develop leaders, correct underperformance and sustain adoption of new tools and operating practices.
* **New product launch experience.** Direct experience leading service readiness for new product introductions, including pilot execution, technical training, launch criteria, field deployment and post-launch performance improvement.
* **Technical service expertise.** Strong knowledge of critical power, telecom, data center, broadband or industrial service operations, with the ability to lead technical specialists and apply OEM requirements, electrical safety principles and relevant codes to field execution.
* **Commercial and analytical judgment.** Ability to connect customer demand and bookings to workforce capacity, revenue, profitability and cash. Strong executive communication, customer escalation management and cross-functional leadership skills.
* **Systems and education.** Proficiency with field service platforms, financial reporting and project management systems such as Procore. Bachelor’s degree in operations, business, engineering, field service management or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
* **Culture:** Build a high-performance culture through workforce planning, leadership development, succession planning, employee engagement, diversity and inclusion initiatives, and retention strategies

**Preferred Qualifications**
============================

Experience in OEM service, critical power, UPS or DC power systems; national account service delivery across the United States and Canada; and development of training or apprenticeship programs. PMP, Lean/Six Sigma or a relevant operations credential, and a master’s degree or advanced professional education, are desirable.

**Work Environment**
====================

Remote role with travel up to 30% to customer locations, field operations and EnerSys facilities. The Senior Director works closely with regional leadership and cross-functional teams and participates in critical customer and operational escalations.

**General Job Requirements**
----------------------------

* This position will work in an office setting, expect minimal physical demands.

Title: Events Operations Manager
Description:

You'll lead the operational planning, quality and delivery of the full Dubai Schools Games competition calendar, making sure every event meets internationally recognised standards of competition management, technical delivery, safety and participant experience. *Budget and commercial management*

* Own event budgets, forecasts and operating costs, controlling spend and improving profitability
* Oversee supplier selection, negotiations and contracts, ensuring clear deliverables and timely fulfilment

*Team leadership*

* Lead, coach and develop an Events Lead and two Events Coordinators
* Set clear priorities and performance expectations, and ensure appropriate coverage across the programme

*Compliance, safety and reporting*

* Ensure all events comply with permits, venue standards, health and safety, risk assessments, insurance and safeguarding requirements
* Monitor participation, KPIs, financial performance and stakeholder feedback, and report regularly with recommendations

* Lead or support other events and initiatives within the school sports ecosystem as needed

* Degree in Events Management, Sports Management, Business, Marketing or a related field (equivalent relevant experience may be considered)

**Experience**

* 8–10 years of relevant event management experience, preferably in sports competitions

* Experience managing senior stakeholders, preferably including sports authorities, schools or public-sector organisations
* Proven experience managing multiple events simultaneously, ideally across different venues

* Strong understanding of sports event operations, competition formats, venue logistics and participant experience

* Event risk assessment, health and safety, incident management and safeguarding

OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation.
  
  
AI-First. Future-Driven. Human-Centered.
  
At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.
  
  
**Role:** Manager, Software Development
  
**Location:** Richmond Hill, ON (Office-based)
  
  
The Manager, Software Development leads the newly formed engineering team delivering the Image& Fax Aviator Platform. This first-line manager will recruit, onboard, coach, and directly manage software engineers and technical specialists working across Java-based cloud services, Python-based AI and document intelligence, React user experiences, enterprise integrations, and platform operations. The role is accountable for day-to-day people leadership, Scrum execution, engineering delivery, quality, and operational readiness. The manager partners with Product Management and the Principal Engineer to translate strategy into executable plans while establishing an inclusive, accountable, and high-performing engineering culture.
  
  
Your Impact
  
  
Engineering Delivery
  
  

* Own day-to-day execution across one or more Scrum teams and translate roadmap priorities into credible sprint and release plans.
* Partner with Product Management to balance customer value, platform foundations, security, reliability, technical debt, and innovation.
* Manage team capacity, dependencies, risks, milestones, and commitments while maintaining clear ownership.
* Ensure increments include code, automated tests, security controls, documentation, observability, deployment automation, and support readiness.
* Provide concise status, risk, staffing, and decision information to senior leadership.
* Escalate material risks early and drive corrective action when scope, staffing, architecture, or dependencies threaten commitments.

People Leadership and Team Building
  
  

* Recruit and onboard the initial eight external hires by the approved target date, then help scale the team to approximately 16 engineers.
* Directly manage engineers and technical specialists, with effective delegation through senior engineers and technical leads.
* Set clear performance expectations and provide frequent coaching, feedback, recognition, and career-development guidance.
* Build an inclusive culture that values customer outcomes, transparency, ownership, collaboration, and technical excellence.
* Partner with Talent Acquisition and HR on requisitions, interview plans, candidate assessment, selection, offers, and onboarding.
* Address performance, engagement, retention, and team-health issues promptly and professionally.

Technical and Operational Leadership
  
  

* Work with the Principal Engineer to establish standards for Java 17+, Spring Boot, Python, React/TypeScript, event-driven services, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, and cloud platforms.
* Maintain enough technical depth to assess tradeoffs, challenge assumptions, support hiring decisions, and remove engineering blockers.
* Drive secure-by-design practices for identity, authorization, tenant isolation, privacy, auditability, APIs, encryption, secrets, and software supply-chain controls.
* Promote automated testing, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, OpenTelemetry, service-level objectives, and production monitoring.
* Ensure architecture and delivery decisions support resilience, scalability, recoverability, cost management, and integration with existing products.
* Lead incident follow-up, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions in a blameless, learning-oriented manner.

Agile and Scrum Leadership
  
  

* Establish consistent Scrum practices including backlog refinement, sprint planning, daily standups, reviews, retrospectives, and release planning.
* Coach engineers and Product Owners on well-formed user stories, acceptance criteria, estimation, Definition of Ready, and Definition of Done.
* Use delivery metrics to improve predictability and flow, not to rank individuals or encourage unhealthy utilization targets.
* Ensure blockers and dependencies are identified early and sprint commitments remain realistic.
* Turn retrospective findings into measurable improvements while avoiding unnecessary ceremony.
* Promote visible work status, shared accountability, and frequent demonstration of working software.

What You Need to Succeed
  
  

* 8+ years of progressively responsible software engineering experience, including 5+ years of direct engineering people leadership.
* Experience directly managing software engineers and technical specialists in a SaaS, cloud-platform, or enterprise-software organization.
* Proven success recruiting and onboarding external engineering talent and building a new or rapidly growing team.
* Demonstrated delivery ownership in Agile/Scrum environments with interdependent product workstreams.
* Strong understanding of cloud-native microservices, distributed systems, APIs, event-driven architecture, containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, observability, and secure development.
* Working knowledge of Java and Spring Boot sufficient to assess candidates, understand design tradeoffs, and guide execution.
* Experience partnering with Product Management on roadmaps, backlogs, release plans, and measurable outcomes.
* Experience coaching employees, managing performance, and handling difficult delivery or organizational situations.
* Clear written and verbal communication with engineers, peers, candidates, and executives.
* Bachelor degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications
  
  

* Experience building a greenfield multi-tenant SaaS platform or standing up a new engineering team.
* Experience directly leading a team of approximately 8 to 16 employees and delegating effectively through senior engineers and technical leads.
* Experience with AI-enabled products, document intelligence, OCR, workflow automation, agents, or human-in-the-loop applications.
* Experience with fax, communications, imaging, healthcare interoperability, content management, or regulated enterprise software.
* Familiarity with Python, React/TypeScript, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Terraform, OpenTelemetry, and a major public cloud.
* Experience managing distributed teams and collaborating across organizational boundaries.
* Relevant cloud, Scrum, Agile, or engineering-management certification.

One Last Thing
  
  
OpenText is more than a corporation—it’s a global community built on trust, character, and purpose. Here, we act ethically, care deeply about people, and always put our clients first. We help teams succeed through collaboration, tackle challenges with resilience, and innovate with intention.
  
  
Join us on our mission to drive positive change through privacy, technology, and teamwork. At OpenText, we don’t just have a culture—we live our values. Choose us because you want to be part of a company that empowers you to make a meaningful impact.
  
  
OpenText's commitment to diversity and inclusion surpasses legal requirements, evident in ourEqual Employment Opportunity Statement of Policy which promotes a respectful and empowering environment for employees of all backgrounds, culture, national origin, race, color, gender, gender identification, sexual orientation, family status, age, veteran status, disability, religion, or other basis protected by applicable laws.
  
  
If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please submit a ticket atAsk HR. Our proactive approach fosters collaboration, innovation, and personal growth, enriching OpenText's vibrant workplace.
  
  
**Compensation:** At OpenText, we offer a thoughtfully designed benefits package that supports your physical, emotional, and financial wellbeing. As you move through the hiring process, we’re happy to provide more details about our compensation programs, including variable and commission compensation opportunities for eligible roles, vacation entitlement, and paid time off.
